solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Despot in a terrible land the other side of the world

definitions.text: land the other side of the world
definitions.note: plural name for lands such as Australia and New Zealand, opposite Britain on the globe

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A tyrant rules over a dreadful country far away on the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges DESPOT IN A; 'land' starts the definition rather than joining the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Britons call Australia and New Zealand by this name, meaning the region diametrically opposite them on the globe.

clue.text: Like marriage fixed by parents? There's a right row with daughter!

parts.note: a range is a row or line, as of mountains
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A family squabble breaks out over a parental match for a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, fitting the surface, but it means a line, as in a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage set up by the parents is described as an arranged one, a set idiom.

clue.text: The difference noticed when we aren't selling enough

definitions.text: The difference noticed when we aren't selling enough

parts.words: The difference noticed when we aren't selling enough
parts.note: a nation buying more from abroad than it sells abroad shows this shortfall in its accounts

explanation.definitionFit: The economic term names the shortfall between a country's imports and its exports.

clue.text: Academic getting with it makes financial gain

parts.note: a prof is a professor, an academic
'it' as in fashionable is a playful reading; here the words 'with it' give IT, the 'with' a mere joining sense

explanation.surface: A trendy professor earns some money on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Money made from a deal beyond its costs is a financial gain, a straight synonym.

clue.text: It gets one routed a different way

definitions.text: It gets one routed a different way

indicators.note: the clue literally tells us the letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A diversion sends traffic along another road.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, and 'routed' put 'a different way' supplies the letters, making it an all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion sends a traveller along an alternative road, which is exactly what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Distributes the last bits, coming in to us randomly

indicators.note: says one piece is entering the middle of the other
letters arranged at random are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: ends are the last bits of something

explanation.surface: Someone hands out the leftover scraps to us at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'randomly' turns TO US into SOUT, and 'coming in' puts ENDS inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To send things out is a phrasal verb for issuing or distributing them.

clue.text: Some mess often swirling around in ditch

indicators.note: something swirling round turns about, so the letters run backwards
only some of the letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A ditch keeps collecting swirling muck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ESSOF from 'mess often'; 'swirling around' turns those letters the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A fosse is a ditch or moat, especially as a defensive trench.

clue.text: Female on estate, one opposing almost all celebration

parts.note: est. is an abbreviation of estate
the Roman numeral I is one
v., versus, means against or opposing

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A woman on a country estate objects to nearly every party.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival is a day or period of celebration, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Blemish in botanical part

definitions.meaning: a mark of disgrace, a blemish on a reputation
in a flower, the ... is the part of the pistil that receives pollen

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mark of shame and the pollen-catching tip of a flower's pistil.

clue.text: English conclusion to luncheon? Possibly apple dish

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the following word

parts.note: an apple is one example of a tree, as signalled by 'possibly'

explanation.surface: Apple pie might round off an English luncheon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apple dish' reads as a pudding, but 'Possibly apple' is the tree and 'dish' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a dish served at a meal, often the main course or one before it.

clue.text: Information from computer that could be dear

parts.note: the word READ, when its letters are put out of order, could give DEAR

explanation.surface: Computer data might turn out to be expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is a common anagram signal, so READ 'out' is wordplay whose result could be 'dear'.
explanation.definitionFit: A readout is the data displayed or printed by a computer or instrument.

clue.text: Hunted animal trapped by senior person with a lot of experience

definitions.text: person with a lot of experience

indicators.note: the first piece is caught inside the second

parts.note: senior means older
the stag is the deer traditionally hunted

explanation.surface: A deer is cornered by an elderly veteran of the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is an informal term for a veteran, someone long experienced in an activity.

clue.text: Hoodlum not having name for being a joker

indicators.note: the following letter is missing from the word

parts.note: a hoodlum is a gangster

explanation.surface: A thug is nameless because he is a prankster.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is someone who tells gags, a joker or comedian.

clue.text: Get rid of old boy having had tea maybe around six

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
VI is six in Roman numerals
tea is one example of a meal, so having had it you ate

explanation.surface: A former pupil finishes his tea at about six and clears off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around six' reads as the time tea is taken in the surface; 'around' is only a link and the Roman six sits between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate is to remove a difficulty or need, to get rid of it in advance.

clue.text: Pal sentenced due to skip part of sentence

indicators.note: skipping about, the letters leap into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend who has been convicted is about to jump bail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' is used in two senses: a court's punishment in the surface and a grammatical unit in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar's term for a subordinate clause, which cannot stand alone and forms part of a sentence.

clue.text: One invader or another seen around the Hastings region

indicators.note: one piece is seen surrounding the other

parts.note: another invader: the Normans invaded England in 1066
Hastings is in south-east England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A Viking or Norman raider appears near Hastings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of Hastings, 1066, was won by the Norman invaders of England; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norseman was a Scandinavian raider, a Viking, so one invader of medieval Britain.

clue.text: City of London still blissful

parts.note: EC, East Central, is the postcode for the City of London
still means motionless, static

explanation.surface: The financial district is calm and content.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overwhelmed with joy, a close synonym of blissful.

clue.text: Woman thought to be like Queen Victoria when grouchy

parts.note: Una is a woman's name
mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: A woman is said to resemble a grumpy Queen Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously credited with the remark 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Her legendary put-down gives the word for not entertained, the queen's supposed state when displeased.

clue.text: Part of book to go totally over to the internet?

definitions.meaning: a leaf pasted inside the cover of a hardback

definitions.text: to go totally over to the internet?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, to finish with printed paper and publish online instead

explanation.definitionFit: The bookbinding term for the leaves inside a cover also reads as a phrase for ceasing print publication.

clue.text: Wants little lad to hug father

indicators.note: one piece embraces the other

parts.note: Des is a short form of the boy's name Desmond
to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A small boy wants to cuddle his dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Desires as a plural noun means wants or wishes.

clue.text: Flying saucer copper observed in East Anglian town

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, in East Anglia
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman reports a UFO in a Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal; DISS is a small Norfolk town.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is a heavy disc thrown in athletics, jokingly a flying saucer.

clue.text: Son to break down, being thin

parts.note: to parse is to break a sentence down into its grammatical parts

explanation.surface: A boy collapses because he is so skinny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break down' suggests collapsing; here it is grammatical analysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly scattered, so thin in the sense of scanty.

clue.text: Map held by boy shows northern region

indicators.note: the first piece is held inside the second

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A young lad carries a map of the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapland is the far-northern region of Scandinavia and Finland.

clue.text: Foam runs under machine

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming after

parts.note: a lathe is a machine tool
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Suds flow beneath a workshop machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lather is the froth formed by soap and water, a kind of foam.

clue.text: Fish I managed to get into kitchen vessel when chopped

indicators.note: the pieces are put inside the vessel
the vessel's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pan is a kitchen vessel
ran means managed, as a business

explanation.surface: A cook gets a fish into a pan after chopping it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when chopped' trims the final letter off the kitchen vessel, and 'to get into' puts the one and the verb inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirana, more often piranha, is a sharp-toothed South American fish.

clue.text: Repair's apt to be tricky without one?

definitions.text: Repair's apt to be tricky without one?

indicators.note: tricky letters are awkward, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A mending job can be awkward if a component is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of REPAIRS APT minus I ('without one') are rearranged; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement component kept in reserve; without it a repair can indeed be awkward.

clue.text: Leads with tails down presumably

parts.note: a tossed coin with its reverse face down shows the other face upward, and the phrase also means a warning given in advance

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal warning, and also what lies uppermost when a coin's tails side is down.

clue.text: Sparkle noticed around hospital

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: seen means noticed

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a glint near the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheen is a soft lustre or shine, close to sparkle.

clue.text: Herb no good for dog and its owner!

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: a corgi is a breed of dog
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen, famously owned corgis

explanation.surface: A herb is useless for a pet and its keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Elizabeth II was famous for her corgis, so the corgi's owner is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is an aromatic herb whose leaves and seeds are used in cooking.
